slides.0.title: Beer
slides.0.subtitle: Malt, hops, yeast and water: four ingredients, countless styles
slides.1.title: Ingredients and fermentation
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Malt
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Malted and kilned barley (or wheat) provides fermentable sugar; the degree of kilning or roasting sets colour and flavour, from pale biscuit to dark coffee and chocolate
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Hops
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Hops add bitterness and aroma (citrus, pine, floral, tropical fruit) and act as a preservative; bitterness is often expressed in IBU
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Ale and lager
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Ale uses top-fermenting yeast at warmer temperatures, giving more fruit and esters; lager uses bottom-fermenting yeast at cool temperatures with cold storage, giving a clean, crisp style. Historically the 1516 Bavarian purity law allowed only water, barley and hops
slides.1.content: Split ale from lager, then look at malt roasting and hops: that is the map of beer styles.
slides.2.title: Main styles and service
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The lager family
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Pilsner originated in Plzeň, Czechia, in 1842: pale gold, hop-forward and crisp; Germany and Czechia also have lagers of different strength and colour such as Helles and Bock
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The ale family
slides.2.highlights.1.content: IPA is strongly hoppy and bitter; stout and porter get coffee and chocolate from roasted barley or dark malt; German wheat beer (Hefeweizen) gets banana and clove from its yeast; Belgian Trappist beers are brewed in monasteries
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Spontaneous fermentation and service
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Belgian lambic ferments spontaneously with airborne wild yeast and bacteria, tart and complex; gueuze blends young and old lambic, kriek adds cherries. For service, lagers are colder (about 3–7°C) and flavourful ales a little warmer (about 7–13°C)
slides.2.content: Beers on a list also need describing and pairing: style, bitterness, alcohol and temperature.
